paragraphs: A reinforcement learning agent that acts from images can struggle when the scene changes visually. This paper identifies two problems in earlier approaches: the agent may assign uneven importance to consecutive frames, and it may rely on particular background regions instead of the objects relevant to its task. Both problems concern which visual information the agent learns to use.

The proposed framework, SimGRL, addresses these problems with two targeted changes. Its image encoder combines frames after extracting their features, rather than stacking the original images together. This modification is intended to reduce the uneven treatment of successive frames. The framework also introduces shifted random overlay augmentation, a training technique designed to reduce reliance on backgrounds under dynamic visual changes.

Experiments report stronger generalization and state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks including the DeepMind Control Suite. The findings support combining changes to temporal representation with visual augmentation: one addresses how information from different frames enters the model, while the other addresses sensitivity to distracting scene content.
neurips-2024-a-simple-framework-for-gene.tldr: SimGRL improves visual reinforcement learning generalization by changing how frames are combined and augmenting scenes to reduce background dependence.

paragraphs: Object detectors use non-maximum suppression, or NMS, to filter competing detections after the network produces its predictions. As the networks themselves become faster, this final processing step can become a significant efficiency bottleneck. The paper studies NMS through graph theory and uses the resulting structural understanding to develop two acceleration methods.

QSI-NMS recursively divides the problem into smaller pieces, accepting a small loss in detection accuracy. Its extended version, eQSI-NMS, achieves the stated optimal complexity of O(n log n). BOE-NMS instead exploits the locality of suppression to improve constant factors without a reported loss in mean average precision, or mAP. The authors also introduce NMS-Bench to support systematic comparison of suppression methods.

With YOLOv8-N on MS COCO 2017, QSI-NMS runs at 6.2 times the speed of the original NMS with a reported 0.1% mAP decrease. eQSI-NMS reaches 10.7 times the speed with a 0.3% decrease, while BOE-NMS reaches 5.1 times the speed without reducing mAP. These results describe improvements to the suppression step in that benchmark setup.
neurips-2024-accelerating-non-maximum-su.tldr: A graph-based analysis of non-maximum suppression yields substantial benchmark speedups with either small or no reported detection-accuracy loss.

paragraphs: An online service may be unable to assign users directly to different treatments. If users choose their own experiences, comparing the resulting groups can confuse treatment effects with preexisting differences between users. This paper studies how a service can instead randomize encouragements that influence treatment choice, then adapt its experiment to identify the best treatment.

The authors formulate this setting as a confounded pure exploration transductive linear bandit problem, using a linear structural equation model. Their algorithms combine experimental design with elimination: evidence gathered during the experiment is used to rule out treatment candidates. A new finite-time confidence interval for an instrumental-variable-style estimator supplies the uncertainty estimates needed for this process despite confounded noise.

The analysis gives sample-complexity upper bounds that nearly match a minimax lower bound, and experiments demonstrate the approach's effectiveness. The contribution is a way to allocate randomized encouragements adaptively when direct treatment assignment is unavailable, while accounting for the bias that would undermine a naive comparison of self-selected groups.
neurips-2024-adaptive-experimentation-wh.tldr: The paper develops adaptive encouragement experiments for identifying the best treatment when direct assignment is unavailable and self-selection creates confounding.

paragraphs: CogVLM is an open-source model that combines image understanding with a pretrained language model. The paper addresses how these two capabilities should interact. A common approach translates image features into the language model's input space, leaving the connection concentrated at the input. CogVLM introduces trainable visual processing inside the model's attention and feed-forward layers.

This visual expert module connects a frozen pretrained language model with an image encoder. Its role is to support deeper interaction between visual and language features across the model's internal processing. The abstract reports that this integration preserves performance on natural language processing tasks, making retention of language capability part of the claimed result alongside improved multimodal understanding.

CogVLM-17B achieves reported state-of-the-art results on 17 cross-modal benchmarks spanning image captioning, visual question answering, broader visual-language evaluation, and visual grounding. These tasks test different uses of image-language integration, from describing a scene to locating a referenced region. Together, the results support the proposed internal visual expert as an effective architecture across the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2024-cogvlm-visual-expert-for-pr.tldr: CogVLM integrates a trainable visual expert into a frozen language model, reporting strong multimodal performance while preserving language-task performance.

paragraphs: Neural methods can solve vehicle routing problems efficiently and reduce dependence on specialized domain knowledge. However, the paper highlights a robustness problem: deliberately crafted changes to routing instances can substantially degrade their performance. Its goal is to strengthen these learned solvers against attacks while also improving their behavior on ordinary, unperturbed instances.

The proposed Collaborative Neural Framework, or CNF, builds an ensemble around a given neural routing method. Multiple models undergo adversarial training collaboratively, so robustness is developed across the group. A separate neural router distributes training instances among those models. This assignment mechanism is designed to balance their workloads and make their collaboration more effective.

Experiments report successful defense against different attacks across multiple neural vehicle routing methods, together with improved generalization on clean instances. The framework also shows strong out-of-distribution generalization on benchmark instances. These findings support coordinated ensemble training as a useful defense strategy for the evaluated routing solvers, with benefits extending beyond performance on the attacked examples themselves.
neurips-2024-collaboration-towards-robus.tldr: CNF collaboratively trains ensembles of neural routing models to improve attack resistance and generalization on clean and out-of-distribution instances.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction attaches uncertainty estimates to model predictions, but applying it to time series is difficult because the usual exchangeability assumption is violated. Observations can change over time in ways that make past errors less representative of current ones. Existing approaches often compensate using manually chosen weights in the output space, which the paper associates with overly conservative predictions.

Conformalized Time Series with Semantic Features, or CT-SSF, moves weight learning into the model's learned representation space. It uses the structure encouraged by deep representation learning to adjust weights dynamically, emphasizing semantic features relevant to the current prediction. This makes the weighting depend on information captured inside the representation rather than only on predicted outputs.

The authors provide a theoretical result favoring CT-SSF over previous output-space methods. Experiments on synthetic and benchmark datasets report substantially better prediction efficiency while retaining a valid coverage guarantee. The stated result addresses the tradeoff between useful uncertainty estimates and coverage: the method aims to reduce unnecessary conservatism without giving up the reported guarantee.
neurips-2024-conformalized-time-series-w.tldr: CT-SSF learns prediction-dependent weights in a semantic representation space to improve time-series conformal prediction efficiency while maintaining valid coverage.

paragraphs: Direct3D generates 3D shapes from images using a model that learns directly in a 3D representation. The paper targets a central obstacle to scaling this task: representing detailed geometry compactly enough for generative learning. Its pipeline does not require a multi-view diffusion model or score distillation sampling optimization.

The first component, D3D-VAE, compresses high-resolution shapes into a continuous latent representation organized as three feature planes. The decoded geometry is supervised directly through a semi-continuous surface sampling strategy, rather than through rendered images. The second component, D3D-DiT, learns the distribution of these compressed shapes and combines positional information from all three planes.

To condition generation on an input image, the pipeline uses both semantic information and pixel-level information. This supports production of shapes consistent with the supplied image. Experiments report better generation quality and generalization than earlier image-to-3D approaches. The findings support the combination of compact geometry encoding, direct geometric supervision, and a diffusion transformer as a scalable approach to the evaluated 3D generation tasks.
neurips-2024-direct3d-scalable-image-to-.tldr: Direct3D combines a geometry-supervised 3D autoencoder with a diffusion transformer to generate image-consistent shapes with improved reported quality and generalization.

paragraphs: Continuous diffusion models must bridge a mismatch when generating discrete data such as language tokens or categorical pixels. The paper identifies missing guidance from the boundaries between discrete outcomes as one major cause of this difficulty. Learning a continuous probability landscape without that guidance can make its eventual discrete outputs less precise.

The proposed method changes the forward diffusion process in two stages. It first estimates a boundary prior, then rescales the forward trajectory to build a diffusion model conditioned on that boundary information. The reverse process is adjusted proportionally as well. Together, these changes aim to align the learned probability contours more closely with the discrete outcomes the model must produce.

Experiments report improvements over earlier continuous diffusion language models on three translation tasks and one summarization task, alongside competitive results against autoregressive transformers. For images, the method achieves results comparable to continuous diffusion models using ordinal pixels and a new reported state of the art for categorical generation on CIFAR-10. These findings support boundary guidance across both language and discrete image generation.
neurips-2024-discrete-modeling-via-bound.tldr: Boundary-conditioned diffusion aligns continuous generation with discrete outcomes, improving reported language and categorical image generation results.

paragraphs: Video masked autoencoders learn representations by reconstructing hidden video content. Extending training to longer clips is expensive because dense self-attention in the decoder consumes substantial memory and computation. This paper tackles that bottleneck by selecting which tokens deserve reconstruction, allowing training on 128 frames instead of the shorter clips common in earlier work.

The proposed LVMAE uses adaptive decoder masking to prioritize important tokens rather than choosing them randomly or uniformly. A MAGVIT-based tokenizer jointly learns the tokens and their priorities, and the reconstruction targets are quantized tokens. The selection strategy therefore links what the decoder reconstructs with a learned assessment of which content matters.

Ablation experiments support the design choices and show improved performance for the 128-frame encoders over 32-frame counterparts. The paper reports gains over the previous state of the art of 3.9 points on Diving48 and 2.5 points on EPIC-Kitchens-100 verb classification. These gains use a simple core architecture and video-only pretraining, demonstrating the value of longer video representations in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-extending-video-masked-auto.tldr: LVMAE learns which video tokens to reconstruct, enabling 128-frame pretraining and improving reported action-recognition performance.

paragraphs: This paper studies distributed reinforcement learning agents that share environment dynamics but have different private reward functions. The agents seek one policy maximizing their combined discounted rewards without exchanging local trajectories. Communication is decentralized: each agent shares information only with neighbors in a prescribed network, making incomplete information exchange part of the optimization problem.

For tabular problems with softmax policies, the authors develop standard and entropy-regularized federated natural policy gradient methods. Gradient tracking helps each agent estimate the global action-value function despite limited communication. Under exact policy evaluation, the analysis establishes global convergence rates that are nearly independent of the number of states and actions, while exposing the effects of network size and connectivity.

The paper also develops a federated natural actor-critic method with function approximation, extending beyond explicit tables of states and actions. Its finite-time sample-complexity analysis accounts for approximation errors. The results thus distinguish a convergence guarantee under exact tabular evaluation from a broader learning method whose analysis explicitly incorporates imperfect function representation.
neurips-2024-federated-natural-policy-gr.tldr: The paper develops decentralized policy optimization methods with global convergence guarantees under exact evaluation and sample-complexity analysis with function approximation.

paragraphs: A cell's response to a drug or genetic perturbation depends on its context, including cell type and genetic background. Understanding this dependence matters because a treatment may affect some cells differently from others. The paper develops Factorized Causal Representation learning, or FCR, to separate treatment effects, contextual effects, and their interactions in single-cell perturbation data.

FCR is a deep generative model with three distinct representations: one for contextual covariates, one for treatment, and one for the interaction between them. Using nonlinear independent component analysis theory, the authors prove component-wise identifiability for the interaction representation and block-wise identifiability for the treatment and context representations. The theoretical distinctions describe different levels at which the learned factors can be identified.

The authors implement the model and report better performance than state-of-the-art baselines on several tasks across four single-cell datasets. The contribution combines empirical usefulness with an analysis of what the separated representations identify. This is particularly relevant to studying treatment responses that vary with cellular context, rather than treating each response as independent of that context.
neurips-2024-learning-identifiable-facto.tldr: FCR separates cellular context, treatment, and interaction representations, with identifiability results and improved performance across four single-cell datasets.

paragraphs: Scientific floating-point datasets contain structure from the processes that generated them, alongside noise associated with truncation and discretization errors. Conventional entropy coding does not fully exploit those generating mechanisms. MeLLoC aims to improve lossless compression by learning high-order physical structure and combining that information with classical encoding.

The method treats the stored values as discrete samples of a physical field described by differential equations. It solves an inverse problem to identify governing-equation coefficients with more compressible numerical representations. This connects the compression process to an inferred description of the underlying field. Periodic extension techniques are also used to accelerate decompression, addressing the computational cost of recovering the data.

Experiments across scientific datasets report consistently better performance than state-of-the-art lossless compressors, with favorable tradeoffs between compression ratio and computational cost. Because the task is lossless, the goal is to reduce storage while recovering the original data exactly. The reported results support using knowledge of data-generating mechanisms as an additional source of compressible structure in scientific computing.
neurips-2024-melloc-lossless-compression.tldr: MeLLoC improves lossless scientific-data compression by learning differential-equation structure and combining it with classical encoding.

paragraphs: Multidimensional scaling represents objects using their pairwise dissimilarities. Neuc-MDS extends this approach so the resulting representation can be non-Euclidean and even non-metric. This flexibility matters when the supplied dissimilarities contain structure that a conventional Euclidean representation does not capture well. The paper changes the geometry available to the method rather than requiring the output to use ordinary distances.

Its central step replaces the usual inner product with more general symmetric bilinear forms. That allows the representation to use negative as well as positive eigenvalues of the dissimilarity Gram matrix. The algorithm efficiently chooses among both kinds of eigenvalues to reduce STRESS, a measure of the summed squared errors in reconstructed pairwise relationships.

The authors analyze reconstruction error and prove optimality for minimizing lower bounds on STRESS. This is a specific theoretical result about those bounds, rather than a stated guarantee of globally minimizing STRESS itself. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets compare Neuc-MDS with linear and nonlinear dimensionality-reduction methods and demonstrate its ability to address previously identified limitations of classical MDS.
neurips-2024-neuc-mds-non-euclidean-mult.tldr: Neuc-MDS uses more general geometry and both positive and negative eigenvalues to better represent pairwise dissimilarities.

paragraphs: Black-box adversarial optimization searches for solutions through queries to a problem whose full structure is unavailable. This paper asks whether some algorithms have an inherent average advantage in that setting. It establishes a No Free Lunch theorem using pure-strategy Nash equilibrium as the solution concept, emphasizing that the definition of a solution is central to the result.

Under the theorem's setup, when cost is measured by the number of payoff-matrix rows and columns queried, all black-box adversarial optimization algorithms have equal average performance. The result concerns that particular solution concept, query accounting, and averaging framework. It does not claim that algorithms perform equally on every individual game.

The authors also introduce a black-box complexity analysis for adversarial optimization. Combining their theorem with Yao's Principle yields lower bounds on the queries needed to find an equilibrium. Examples involving two-player zero-sum games illustrate the consequences, and the paper states a linear query lower bound for general bimatrix games with a unique equilibrium. These results characterize limits on what query-based methods can achieve.
neurips-2024-no-free-lunch-theorem-and-b.tldr: The paper proves a No Free Lunch theorem for black-box equilibrium search under specified query costs and derives query-complexity lower bounds.

paragraphs: Best-arm identification asks an algorithm to find the option with the highest mean reward to a specified accuracy. In the multi-fidelity version, it can buy cheaper but less accurate observations instead of always paying for the highest fidelity. The challenge is to choose both which option to investigate and how much precision each observation should provide.

The paper derives a tight lower bound on the total cost required, with the bound depending on the particular problem instance. This sharpens earlier bounds that left algorithmic optimality unclear. Studying the optimization problem inside the bound then guides the design of a computationally efficient, gradient-based algorithm with asymptotically optimal cost complexity.

Experiments show benefits over existing methods, complementing the theoretical cost analysis. The work also provides insight into an optimal fidelity for each arm, linking the value of an observation's precision to the option being assessed. Its optimality claim is asymptotic: the algorithm's cost approaches the theoretical benchmark in the analyzed limiting regime.
neurips-2024-optimal-multi-fidelity-best.tldr: A tight cost lower bound leads to an asymptotically optimal algorithm for identifying the best option using observations of different costs and fidelities.

paragraphs: Several models can achieve similarly strong accuracy while making different predictions for particular cases. This Rashomon effect creates opportunities to choose models with desirable fairness or interpretability properties, but it also makes individual decisions sensitive to model choice. The paper investigates this tension in gradient boosting, a widely used approach for tabular data.

The authors develop theoretical derivations and an information-theoretic characterization of the Rashomon set, the collection of competing well-performing models. They also introduce RashomonGB, an inference technique for inspecting this effect efficiently in practice. The method supports estimating predictive multiplicity and selecting models subject to group fairness constraints, connecting the analysis to concrete model-selection decisions.

Across more than 20 datasets, RashomonGB outperforms existing baselines in estimating multiplicity metrics and selecting models under fairness constraints. The paper additionally proposes a framework for reducing predictive multiplicity and demonstrates its effectiveness empirically. Together, these contributions address both understanding disagreement among accurate gradient-boosting models and reducing the resulting instability in their predictions.
neurips-2024-rashomongb-analyzing-the-ra.tldr: RashomonGB analyzes disagreement among accurate gradient-boosting models, improves fairness-constrained model selection, and supports reducing predictive multiplicity.

paragraphs: Multi-view clustering groups data using information from different sources or representations. Contrastive methods learn from pairs designated as matching or nonmatching, but both designations can be wrong. Unrelated observations may be mistakenly paired across views, while randomly selected negative pairs may actually belong to the same cluster. The paper calls this combination dual noisy correspondence.

CANDY addresses the two errors through different mechanisms. It uses similarities between views as contextual evidence for detecting false negatives, where related samples have been treated as unrelated. A spectral module then refines correspondences to reduce the damage caused by false positives. The method therefore works on the reliability of the pair relationships used during learning.

Experiments on five multi-view benchmarks compare CANDY with eight competing clustering methods and support its effectiveness against this combined noise problem. The approach matters because correcting only mismatched positive pairs would leave misleading negative pairs in place. The reported results support treating both sources of correspondence error within one clustering framework.
neurips-2024-robust-contrastive-multi-vi.tldr: CANDY improves contrastive multi-view clustering by addressing both falsely matched pairs and related samples mistakenly used as negatives.

paragraphs: A third-party machine learning service may contain a backdoor, while its users lack access to training data or model internals. SampDetox tackles this black-box setting by purifying inputs before inference. Diffusion-based purification adds noise to disrupt a backdoor and then reconstructs the sample, but excessive noise can also destroy the content needed for a correct prediction.

A preliminary study finds that low-visibility backdoors are vulnerable to weak noise, whereas high-visibility backdoors require stronger noise but are easier to detect. SampDetox uses this distinction in stages. It first applies weak noise, then compares the reconstructed sample with the original using structural similarity to locate conspicuous backdoor regions. Stronger noise is concentrated on those regions.

This localized treatment aims to remove visible triggers while preserving the sample's overall semantic content. The purified inputs can then be submitted even to a poisoned model. Experiments report effective defense against several state-of-the-art backdoor attacks, supporting the strategy of matching perturbation strength and location to the backdoor characteristics observed in the study.
neurips-2024-sampdetox-black-box-backdoo.tldr: SampDetox purifies inputs with weak global noise and stronger localized noise to defend against backdoors without accessing model internals.

paragraphs: Visual grounding identifies the image region described by a sentence. The paper argues that methods learning image-text fusion mainly from limited downstream data struggle with complex expressions. SimVG addresses this by drawing on multimodal pretraining, allowing the grounding system to use visual-language interactions learned beyond its task-specific training examples.

The framework separates visual-language feature fusion from the downstream grounding task. It uses existing multimodal pretrained models and adds object tokens to connect pretrained representations with task-specific learning. During joint training of multiple branches, a dynamic weighting scheme distills information into a simpler branch. That branch consists only of a lightweight multilayer perceptron, reducing structural complexity and improving inference speed.

Experiments on six visual grounding datasets report new state-of-the-art performance alongside improvements in efficiency and convergence speed. The findings support combining broadly pretrained multimodal features with a compact downstream predictor. The distillation component is central to that combination: it is designed to strengthen the lightweight branch's representations while retaining the simpler structure used for faster reasoning.
neurips-2024-simvg-a-simple-framework-fo.tldr: SimVG combines pretrained image-text fusion with distillation into a lightweight grounding branch, improving reported accuracy, efficiency, and convergence speed.

paragraphs: LiDAR segmentation assigns semantic labels to points so robots can interpret their surroundings. Many methods project the point cloud into a two-dimensional image for processing, but multiple points can land at the same image position. Keeping only one discards geometric information, which can be especially damaging when representing small objects.

SFCNet replaces that single-point storage with a spherical frustum structure that retains all points mapped to each position. A hash-based representation makes this storage more memory-efficient. The authors also introduce sparse convolution and farthest-point sampling operations adapted to the frustums, allowing the network to process and sample the retained points while using two-dimensional convolutional networks.

On SemanticKITTI and nuScenes, SFCNet outperforms earlier projection-based segmentation methods using conventional spherical projection. It also reports better small-object segmentation, linked to preserving more complete geometry. The contribution targets a specific information loss caused by projection collisions: its representation keeps the points that conventional projection would discard before the segmentation network can use them.
neurips-2024-spherical-frustum-sparse-co.tldr: SFCNet retains all LiDAR points sharing a projected position, improving reported segmentation performance, particularly for small objects.

paragraphs: Objects made of scattering materials are difficult to reconstruct and relight because light travels beneath their surfaces. Gaussian splatting efficiently represents visible surfaces, but that representation alone does not capture the volumetric behavior of subsurface scattering. This paper combines a Gaussian surface model with a separate representation of the internal scattering component.

The method uses multi-view observations captured with one light active at a time. It jointly estimates object shape and radiance transfer, representing the surface with 3D Gaussians and spatially varying reflectance, while modeling scattering through an implicit volume. A learned incident light field accounts for shadows. All parameters are optimized together using differentiable rendering with ray tracing.

The resulting system supports material editing, relighting, and novel-view synthesis at interactive rates. The authors demonstrate it on synthetic data and contribute a multi-view, multi-light dataset captured in a light stage. Comparisons report similar or better results than previous work with substantially less optimization and rendering time, while allowing detailed control over material properties.
neurips-2024-subsurface-scattering-for-g.tldr: A hybrid Gaussian-surface and volumetric-scattering model enables interactive relighting and material editing from multi-view, one-light-at-a-time captures.

paragraphs: Models that rely on misleading correlations can perform poorly on minority groups even when their overall accuracy looks strong. This paper examines how finetuning choices affect worst-group accuracy across four vision and language benchmarks. Its central finding is that familiar techniques such as class balancing interact with training and group structure in unexpectedly nuanced ways.

Mini-batch upsampling and loss upweighting can cause worst-group accuracy to decline over training epochs, eventually doing no better than omitting class balancing. Creating a balanced subset by removing data can work better in some settings, but its success depends on the groups present. The authors propose a mixture method that can outperform both approaches. Larger pretrained models generally help when paired with appropriate balancing.

The paper also identifies spectral imbalance in learned features as a possible contributor to disparities: within classes, minority-group covariance matrices have larger spectral norms than majority-group matrices. This is presented as a potential explanation. Overall, the empirical results show that group robustness depends on the details of balancing, scaling, and representation during finetuning.
neurips-2024-the-group-robustness-is-in-.tldr: Experiments show that finetuning robustness depends on how class balancing, model scale, and group structure interact, with standard balancing sometimes hurting worst-group accuracy.

paragraphs: Gaze-following systems typically predict the location in an image where a person is looking. A coordinate or heatmap answers where the gaze lands, but it does not directly identify the kind of target receiving attention. This paper extends the task to predict both the target's location and its semantic label.

The authors introduce an architecture that produces these two outputs together. To support training and evaluation, they build a pseudo-annotation pipeline for the GazeFollow dataset, introduce a new benchmark, define an experimental protocol, and construct a comparison baseline. These additions make recognition of the gaze target an explicit part of the task rather than leaving it outside the localization evaluation.

The method reports a new state of the art for localization on the main GazeFollow benchmark and competitive recognition results on both evaluated datasets, using 40% fewer parameters than the baseline. The findings suggest that adding semantic target prediction can coexist with strong localization in a smaller model, giving gaze-following outputs a more directly interpretable meaning.
neurips-2024-toward-semantic-gaze-target.tldr: The paper extends gaze following to predict both where a person looks and the target's semantic label, with strong results using fewer parameters.

paragraphs: A controller and a robot may temporarily lose communication in both directions. During such an interruption, the controller cannot receive new states or send new actions. This paper formalizes that situation as an Intermittent Control Markov Decision Process, where an agent sends a sequence of future actions before communication becomes unavailable.

Learning to generate several actions directly in the original action space can make exploration difficult and produce unnatural motion. The proposed Multi-step Action Representation, or MARS, encodes action sequences into a compact latent space that can be decoded back into executable actions. Mainstream reinforcement learning methods can then learn policies using this sequence representation, with the aim of producing smoother and more efficient motion.

Experiments in simulation and real-world robotic grasping report substantial improvements in learning efficiency and final performance over existing baselines. The findings support representing a planned sequence as a compact learnable unit when step-by-step interaction is unavailable. This directly addresses how the executor can continue moving during the communication gaps modeled by the paper.
neurips-2024-unlock-the-intermittent-con.tldr: MARS learns compact representations of action sequences so reinforcement learning controllers can operate more effectively through communication interruptions.

paragraphs: Generative time-series models often specialize in either short or long sequences. The paper links this split to difficulties such as recurrent-network gradients, transformer computation costs, and limited expressiveness in state space models. It proposes a common framework that first transforms a time series into an image-like representation, making image diffusion models available for sequence generation.

The method uses invertible transformations, including delay embedding and the short-time Fourier transform. Invertibility connects generated image representations back to time series. This design combines access to advanced visual diffusion models with established techniques for representing temporal data as images, while supporting both short and long inputs within the same framework.

Evaluation covers unconditional generation, interpolation, and extrapolation, with reported state-of-the-art results against strong baselines. For unconditional generation, the abstract reports mean improvements over previous diffusion models of 58.17% in the short-sequence discriminative score and 132.61% in long and ultra-long classification scores. These are improvements in the named evaluation scores, supporting the representation strategy across the tested sequence lengths and tasks.
neurips-2024-utilizing-image-transforms-.tldr: Invertible time-series-to-image transformations let one diffusion framework generate short and long sequences with strong reported results across several tasks.
